Sweep Backtest (SBT)

5760 optimizer configurations over one FIXED curation (data/cbt_3yr_v10) · no LLM, no re-curation · knobs from investor_profile.backtest.md

1. Parameter settings

The 7 FREE swept knobs — every combination is a cell, 2×4×3×4×3×5×4 = 5760 configs — and the values considered. These knobs only RE-WEIGHT a fixed set of curator picks, which is what makes the grid free: no LLM call is made and no event is discovered or closed differently. Every other optimizer / curator parameter is held at its investor_profile.backtest.md value.

parametervalues sweptcurrent (profile)
cull_ranktrend, keep-firsttrend
max_watchlist4, 6, 8, 126
concentration_cap0.25, 0.4, 0.60.4
lookback_period_days21, 30, 45, 6060
drop_unfunded_weeks0, 2, 40
risk_aversion0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.03.0
min_trade_size0.0, 0.025, 0.05, 0.10.05

2. Return vs drawdown

The horizontal axis is max drawdown — the book's biggest peak-to-trough loss as a fraction of its running peak; further right = deeper loss. The vertical axis is annualized return, so upper-left is best. Each point is one config; colour is the share of the winners' gains handed back by the losers, so a pale point in the upper-left is the whole objective at once. The live config is the purple ★ star.

3. Return vs L1 churn

Same points, risk axis replaced by L1 churn = annualized one-way turnover (Σ|Δweight| across rebalances, ×100/yr): how much of the book is traded per year. Weights are held flat between rebalances, so drift never counts as a trade. Trading is free in an IRA, so read this as stability, not cost: lower churn = less noise-chasing and less overfit, making upper-left the sweet spot.

4. Return vs L2 course correction

Same idea, but the path length the book was dragged through weight-space (√ΣΔweight² per rebalance, summed and annualized). Against L1 it weights concentrated single-name rotations more heavily. The useful read is whether the two norms rank configs alike — if they do, the churn ordering is robust rather than an artefact of which norm was picked.

5. Return vs cancellation

The fourth view of the same points, and the one that matters most: the horizontal axis is the share of the winners' gains handed back by the losers, so upper-left is best — a book that earns and keeps it. Colour is max drawdown, so a pale upper-left point earns well, keeps it, and does so without a deep hole. The cloud's shape is itself the finding: if it were a tight rising diagonal these knobs would only be trading return against cancellation, and it is not one.

6. Recommended settings

Ranked by plateau = ½·the config's own cancellation + ½·the mean of its grid neighbours (every cell one step away on one axis). A lone in-sample spike with weak surroundings sinks below a broad, shallow region — the anti-overfit rank, and the right one here because the best raw cell out of 5,760 on a single 3-year path is very likely noise. Cancellation (the share of the winners' gains the losers hand back) is the objective; Sharpe and Gain/Pain (Schwager: total return ÷ the sum of every down-move) are there to catch a config that cancels little only because it barely traded. Current live config on the bottom row.

7. risk_aversion × drop_unfunded_weeks

Median cancellation at each combination of the two knobs whose marginals span the widest range. This is the panel a 1-D sweep cannot produce, and it is where the interactions hide — a value that looks harmless on average can be the worst choice in one corner of the grid.

8. Each knob on its own

For every value of every knob: the MEDIAN cancellation across all cells holding that value (the bar) and the BEST single cell (the dot). A wide gap between them means the knob only pays in combination with something else. The live setting is outlined.
